title: Moving Day
subtitle: Wednesday 20 April to Monday 2 May 1927: The Inquest at Gale, the Cap Under Guard, the Last Night, and Noon on Shumate Ridge

setting.name: Ottway, Gale and Shumate Ridge, the last eleven days of April 1927
setting.description: The party have brought Dewey Spradlin out, or written his name under Lester Gaither's; they have Lafe Combs's notes, the inspector's notebook, the ledger, and the rule that ends it: the room where it began must be opened to the sun. The company knows what they have. Philadelphia telegraphs: recover all material from 7 North, reopen on 2 May as scheduled. Captain Kincaid posts six men on the concrete cap on Shumate's pasture and the sheriff swears out an injunction against trespass on company openings. Dr. Ketterly, as deputy coroner, can convene an inquest on Lester Gaither's body at Gale, and put 1919 on the record under oath. Every family that has not signed the new contract is to be put on the road on Saturday 30 April, moving day, and Mavis Shumate offers her pasture for their tents, which puts the whole union camp around the cap. There are three clear noons left: Friday 22 April, Thursday 28 April and Sunday 1 May. On Monday 2 May the company's crew goes into 7 North.
setting.atmosphere: Rain, then wind, then a hard bright cold Sunday. The hollow emptying: wagons, Della's Ford, a borrowed coal truck, bedsteads on the road, a cow led up the ridge road on a rope. Tents going up on Shumate's pasture in the rain and smoke from forty cook fires; and on Saturday afternoon every child in the camp sent down the valley in Della's truck and on the Gale train to relatives and church halls in the next county, so that no child is in Ottway or on the ridge for the last night or the noon. Ironwood men in slickers round a concrete slab with a tarpaulin over it. Reporters in Gale: the Banner, a man from the Charleston Gazette, a wire-service stringer from Huntington, and Frankie's editor, Sol Abramowitz, off the Friday train in a bowler hat. On the last night, every light in the camp burning, and the dark outside it total.

keyLocations.name: Gale: the Inquest and the Wire
keyLocations.description: The Selden County courthouse, its second-floor courtroom with tall windows and a pressed-tin ceiling; the jail behind; the Western Union office at the depot, whose operator shows the sheriff every press telegram; the Banner's office; and the depot, where the Huntington train leaves at 7:10 every morning with the mail.
features: A deputy coroner may convene an inquest on any body in the county, empanel six jurors and compel witnesses: Dr. Ketterly can call one on Lester Gaither for Wednesday 27 April, and the sheriff cannot stop it

The Western Union operator: the party's photographs and copy of the notes will be read by the sheriff, and by Kincaid, before they leave Gale by wire; by train, in an envelope, they get to Pittsburgh in a day, if no one searches the mail sack
The jail: Angelo Marchetti and Hobart Lilly, released on the sheriff's order the day Lester Gaither's body is brought to Gale
encounters: Ironwood men at the depot searching the outbound mail sack on Kincaid's order (Night Watchman x2); Della's Ford and the back road over the mountain to the next county's railroad are the other way
The inquest itself: the coroner's jury, six Selden County men, three of them on company retainer; the company's lawyer from Charleston, Garrett Ketterly, Clement's father
secrets: Garrett Ketterly comes up to Gale to represent the company at his own son's inquest. He takes Clement to dinner at the hotel the night before and asks him, gently, to adjourn it. Then he asks him what he has found. Clement's answer, and what he does on the 27th, is the Family Name trait's cost come due

Under oath, at the inquest: Lonzo Cutright tells the truth if he is called; Hobart Lilly tells it whether he is called or not; Inspector Overbey's notebook is already in the county's own file; Lafe Combs's notes, in Frankie's photographs or the cut timbers, are evidence the jury can see. The jury's verdict on Lester Gaither ('died of exposure in the sealed area of Ottway No. 3, having entered it by means unknown') clears the jailed men. The jury may add a rider about 1919 if the party make the case: 'The jury recommends that the State reopen the inquest into the deaths of October 1919.' Persuasion DC 15 with the evidence, DC 20 without the notes
Sol Abramowitz will print anything Frankie can prove, and nothing she can't: the notes, the notebook and the ledger, together, are proof

keyLocations.name: The Company Office
keyLocations.description: Bledsoe's office, with the red-hatched map on the wall and the telegram in the drawer, and across the yard Kincaid's shanty with the new orders on the desk.
features: Philadelphia's telegram to Kincaid, Thursday 21 April: 'RECOVER ALL MATERIAL FROM 7N BEFORE REOPENING. HOLD ALL COMPANY OPENINGS. REOPEN 2 MAY AS SCHEDULED. J.R.O.'
The new contract, with three hundred and eleven signatures and two hundred and four blanks
The company's notice of eviction for Saturday 30 April, posted at the store, the lamp house and the depot
encounters: Bledsoe, alone, every evening, at his desk with the lamp off
secrets: Bledsoe's last choice: he can hand over the 1919 telegram (CLUE E7) to the party or to the inquest, which ends his career and possibly his liberty; he can resign and go to Altoona; or he can do what Philadelphia orders. He will do the first if someone he respects asks him to, and if he is not alone when they ask. If he was taken in bd-scenario-003 and carried out, he does it on the stretcher

Kincaid's last choice: he has his orders, and he has lost men to something that is not the union. If the party saved any of his guards on Thursday 14 April or in 7 North, or brought Lester Gaither out, he will not fire on the camp; he will hold the cap until he is relieved, and then stand aside. If they did none of these, he will do what he is told, and the GM should make that frightening

keyLocations.name: The Rows on Moving Day
keyLocations.description: Saturday 30 April: every company house of a man who has not signed the new contract is emptied onto the road by Ironwood men and deputies from Gale, two hundred and four families, from first light to dark. The Local organises it like a shift change: Della's Ford and a borrowed coal truck run families and furniture up the ridge road to Shumate's pasture all day. Lettie Burchett, whose husband is dead and who signed nothing, is evicted from the last house on Number Two Bottom, and the knocking under her kitchen floor goes on in the empty house.
features: Two hundred families on the road with their goods, in the rain
Mount Moriah and St. Stephen's, company lots both, served notice too; Rev. Greer refuses to leave the church, and so does the priest at St. Stephen's, Father Tibor Kovács
encounters: Ironwood men and Gale deputies carrying furniture (Night Watchman, Deputy Sheriff): it is their job and they do it, some roughly and some carefully, and one or two of them quietly carry a sewing machine all the way up the ridge road for an old woman and walk back down without a word
A confrontation at Mount Moriah, where Rev. Greer stands in the door and a deputy has a warrant
secrets: If the party stand with the families all day, Union Trust reaches 5 by evening whatever it was, and the camp will do what the party ask on Sunday
At dusk, the company banks the coke ovens and cuts the electric plant to everything but Silk Stocking Row and the drift mouth. It is the last night

keyLocations.name: The Last Night
keyLocations.description: Saturday 30 April, dusk to dawn. The rows are half empty and dark; the ovens are banked; the camp is on Shumate's pasture in tents, and at Mount Moriah and St. Stephen's, which have refused to be emptied. The Dark knows what the party mean to do at noon. Unless the Kept Light is burning, it comes up out of the drift mouth at nightfall and goes everywhere that is dark, looking for anyone alone.
features: The pasture: forty tents in a ring round the fenced cap, cook fires, lanterns, the six Ironwood men at the cap with their own lantern, and the woods black all round
Mount Moriah: two hundred people inside, every lamp lit, Rev. Greer at the pulpit, the door open
Silk Stocking Row: the only street lamps in Ottway, and one house dark, Bledsoe's
encounters: The Hungry Dark (adversaries.json), all night: at full strength, and knowing. It uses the voice of everyone it has taken, one after another. It goes for the lone: a guard at the cap who steps out of the lantern light to relieve himself, Bledsoe alone in his dark house, Imre walking back alone to his lamp house to keep the Kept Light, Harley Mabe alone in the lamp house, any player who goes off alone to do one last thing. Make it the longest night of the campaign: a sequence of near things, voices, lamps going blue, a tent whose lantern goes out with three old loaders in it, who are together and safe, and terrified, and the party running toward each voice in pairs

If the Kept Light is relit and burning: the night is quiet on the surface, and the danger is below; anyone who goes into No. 3 tonight, including the company's advance men sent by Kincaid to start 'recovering material' in 7 North a day early, meets it
secrets: Bring Bledsoe in. If the party go down to Silk Stocking Row and fetch the superintendent out of his dark house to Mount Moriah, where two hundred of the people he has lied to for eight years are sitting up together with every lamp lit, Rev. Greer gives him a seat by the stove. In the morning he gives them the telegram, and he walks up the ridge with them

Garland Hensley's choice: if he is still wearing the Ironwood badge, Kincaid posts him at the cap with five other men. Tonight his brother Rad is in the tent nearest the wire. At some point in the night one of the five, Coy Dillard or another, steps out of the light, alone, and Garland has to decide whether to leave his post

CLUE F2, if not yet found: at first light the dark drains up the ridge from the bottom of the hollow to the cap like water to a drain, the frost ring whitens, and the Corpse Light goes out. It has gone home. It lies in its room by day

keyLocations.name: Noon on Shumate Ridge
keyLocations.description: Sunday 1 May, clear and cold and bright, the last clear noon before the company goes in. The concrete cap in the upper pasture, fourteen feet square and two feet thick, stamped O.S.C.Co. 10-17-19, a tarpaulin over it, a fallen fence round it, six Ironwood men, and two hundred miners and their families standing round it with sledges, bars, a borrowed pier glass from the store's furniture floor, and nothing else.
features: Breaking the cap: six hours with sledges and bars for six people working in relays from first light (Heavy Work gives advantage), or a Sapper's charge laid at the cracked corner, after venting the firedamp that has gathered under the lid for eight years through a drill hole for an hour (Mechanics DC 12 to know; DC 13 to place the charge to break the slab without bringing the shaft timbers down)
Under the cap: the shaft, eight feet square, two hundred and twelve feet straight down, the old ladderway rotted out, cold air coming up

The mirror: a six-foot pier glass from the store, two men to hold it, set at the collar on a frame of fence posts and angled to the sun between eleven and one; holding it steady in the wind for a minute is a DEX check DC 12 with help, and a spot of sunlight the size of a dinner table goes down the shaft onto the floor of the barricade room
encounters: Kincaid and six Ironwood men at the cap, with the sheriff's injunction (Deputy Sheriff, Night Watchman x6), and two hundred people in front of them. Whether this is a fight depends on everything that has happened since 8 April. If it becomes one, it is a massacre waiting to happen, and the party are the only people on the ridge who can stop it

The Hungry Dark, below, at noon: it cannot come up into the sun. It knows. When the cap breaks, every lamp on the ridge and in No. 3 goes blue at once, and up the shaft, out of the black, comes Dewey's voice, and Lester's, and the fourteen's, and Lafe Combs's, all at once, calling. Fear check DC 20 for everyone on the pasture
secrets: Mavis's deed: the 1898 conveyance her grandfather signed reserves to the company 'such shafts and openings as it may require, the same to be fenced', and then, in the clause nobody in the family could read, provides that 'any such opening abandoned by the company for ten years shall revert with the surface to the grantor and his heirs'. The Number Two shaft was abandoned in 1916, and the company's own map says so. The cap has been Shumate property since 1926. Educated's Seen It in a Book, Frankie's Morgue and the Wire or Dr. Ketterly's father can read it; the sheriff's injunction is void on its face, and Sizemore, shown it, is glad to say so and go home

THE LAYING (Rule 6): when the sunlight from the glass touches the floor of the barricade room, there is a sound up the shaft like a long breath let out. Every lamp in Ottway No. 3 and on the ridge burns yellow and steady. The voices stop. Everyone present drops to 0 Dread. Anyone below in the room sees the sun on the coal for the first time in eight years, and nothing else. It is over

THE FOURTEEN: after the laying, the shaft is open, and the fourteen can be brought up into daylight by a windlass, one by one, as Lafe Combs would have wanted, with their names said at the collar, and buried in the camp's cemetery, or carried home: Ezell Pettaway by his brother to Hale County, József Kertész by Imre. Each is laid as a Shade when buried under its name by someone who knew who it was, and the knocking under Number Two Bottom stops

synopsis: The last act is not a fight with the Dark, which cannot be beaten by fighting, but a fight for the noon sun on a ridge-top slab of concrete, and for whether a divided company town can stand together long enough to win it. With the notes, the notebook, the ledger and Lester Gaither's body, the party can do three things at once and must choose how to spend eleven days: get the truth out of Selden County past a sheriff who reads every telegram; use Dr. Ketterly's office as deputy coroner to call an inquest on Gaither in Gale and put 1919 on the record under oath against the company's lawyer, who is Clement's own father; and break the cap on Shumate's pasture at a clear noon and throw the sun down the shaft with a mirror, against an injunction and six Ironwood rifles. Philadelphia orders Kincaid to hold every company opening and recover all material from 7 North before the company's crew goes in on 2 May. On Saturday 30 April, moving day, two hundred families are put on the road and carry their goods up the ridge to tents on Shumate's pasture, round the cap; the company banks the ovens and cuts the plant; and the Dark, which knows, has its last night in Ottway. On Sunday, the last clear noon, it comes down to the people on the ridge, a borrowed pier glass, an old deed, and whether Captain Kincaid's men will fire.
hook: Wednesday 20 April, early. Dewey Spradlin is in the four-bed infirmary behind the store under three blankets with his wife's hand in his and his eyes open, or his name is chalked on a timber under Lester Gaither's a mile inside the mountain. Either way, in the next bed, under a sheet, is Lester Gaither, and the sheriff of Selden County has been sent for. On Dr. Ketterly's desk, among the bandages, there are forty photographs drying on a string, of chalk on black timber. At seven the Western Union boy comes up from the depot with a telegram for Captain Kincaid, and Kincaid reads it on the store porch, and folds it, and puts it in his pocket, and sends six men with rifles up the ridge road to Shumate's. Up on the pasture, at noon, the sun comes out for a quarter of an hour for the first time in a week, and Mavis Shumate, standing at the wire with her rifle, watches the shadow of the fence move across the concrete and does arithmetic.

conclusions.conclusion: The cap on Shumate's pasture belongs to the Shumates, not the company, and the sheriff's injunction is void: the 1898 deed's reversion clause and the company's own 1916 abandonment.
clues: The company map's 'No. 2 A.S. abandoned 1916' (the company office)
Frankie's or Clement's reading of the clause (anywhere)

conclusions.conclusion: The Dark is laid by sunlight on the floor of the barricade room at noon on a clear day, thrown down the opened shaft with a mirror; nothing else will do it, and it knows (Rule 6).
clues: F2: the dawn drain to the cap (Shumate's pasture)
F4: Old Lore, Hunter of the Uncanny or Imre's Collector clue (any)

acts.title: The Truth Gets Out
acts.description: Wednesday 20 to Thursday 28 April. The point of this act is to let the party turn evidence into consequences: freeing the jailed men, getting the story past the sheriff and onto the wire, and the inquest at Gale, which is the campaign's one public reckoning with 1919. It is also the act in which the company closes its fist: the cap under guard, the injunction, the eviction notices. The two clear noons in it, Friday 22 and Thursday 28, are chances to finish early, against the guards and the law, before the town is ready.
objectives: Bring Lester Gaither's body to Gale and get Angelo Marchetti and Hobart Lilly released
Get Frankie's story and photographs out of Selden County
Call the inquest, and survive Garrett Ketterly
Find a way past the guards and the injunction on the cap

scenes.name: The Mail Sack
scenes.description: Frankie's photographs of the notes, the inspector's notebook and the ledger, and her copy, must get to Pittsburgh. The Western Union operator shows every press telegram to the sheriff; Kincaid's men search the outbound mail sack at the Gale depot. Options: Della's Ford over the mountain at night to the next county's railroad, with the Ironwood car at the dead line; Garland's badge on the morning train; Dr. Ketterly's father's own law-firm envelope, which nobody would dare open; a miner's wife going to visit her sister in Huntington with the film sewn in her coat. Any of them works with a plan; none of them works without one.
scenes.readAloud: The Gale depot at ten to seven in the morning: the Huntington train breathing steam at the platform, the mail clerk throwing sacks into the car, and two men in Ironwood khaki at the end of the platform with the outbound sack open on a handcart between them, going through it letter by letter. One of them holds an envelope up to the light. The other one is watching the platform. He sees you, and nods, pleasantly, the way you nod to a neighbour.

skillChecks.success: The film goes through. By Friday Sol Abramowitz has it, and by Monday the wire has it.
skillChecks.failure: The envelope is found and confiscated 'for evidence'. Company Suspicion +1. There are more prints; there must be another way.

skillChecks.success: (Della's Ford, over the mountain at night with no lights.) Over the top and down to the next county's railroad by four in the morning; the Ironwood car never knew.
skillChecks.failure: The Ford goes into the ditch on the switchbacks. Everyone takes 2d6 bludgeoning and the film is wet but safe; it is a long walk.

scenes.name: The Inquest at Gale
scenes.description: Wednesday 27 April, ten in the morning, the second-floor courtroom. Dr. Ketterly presides as deputy coroner, with six jurymen; the company's counsel is Garrett Ketterly; the room is full of miners in their Sunday clothes, guards, the Banner, a Charleston reporter and Sol Abramowitz. The witnesses the party call: Garland Hensley on 25 March; Clement himself on the body; Lonzo Cutright; Hobart Lilly; Lettie, on Wash; Morris, on his brother; the notes, the notebook, the ledger, the telegram if Bledsoe has given it. Garrett Ketterly is excellent and kind and destroys any witness who is not sure. The verdict on Gaither clears the jailed men; the rider recommending the State reopen 1919 is the prize.
scenes.readAloud: The courtroom is hot and too full and smells of wet wool and floor polish. Tall windows, a pressed-tin ceiling, a portrait of a judge with side whiskers, six men in a row on the jury bench turning their hats in their hands. At the counsel table on the left a silver-haired man in a beautiful grey suit rises, buttons his coat, and smiles up at the coroner's chair with real affection. 'Doctor,' he says. 'Gentlemen. I appear for the Ottway Smokeless Coal Company. And I want to say, before we begin, how very proud I am of the young man presiding.' Behind him, in the front row, a grey neat man sits with his hands flat on his knees and does not look up.

skillChecks.success: With the notes before them, the jury add their rider. A Selden County coroner's jury asks the State of West Virginia to reopen the deaths of October 1919. It has never happened before.
skillChecks.failure: The verdict clears Angelo and Hobart, and the rider dies on a vote of four to two. The truth is on the record, and the record says nothing about it.

skillChecks.success: (On Garrett Ketterly.) He did not know. He drafted the 1919 inquest's company statement from what Bledsoe told him, and he is finding out now, in this room, in front of his son.
skillChecks.failure: A very good lawyer doing his job.

scenes.name: The Clause Nobody Could Read
scenes.description: Mavis's grandfather's deed of 1898, which she has carried all campaign: a long, close-written conveyance of coal rights in a county clerk's copperplate. Anyone with Seen It in a Book, the Morgue and the Wire, legal training or Dr. Ketterly's father's patience can read the reversion clause (see Noon on Shumate Ridge's secrets) and set it against the company's own map, which marks No. 2 A.S. 'abandoned 1916'. The cap is Shumate property. The injunction is void. The sheriff, shown it, is visibly relieved, rescinds his order, and goes home to Gale; the Ironwood men remain, on company orders, with no law behind them.
scenes.readAloud: Mavis unfolds the deed on Lettie's table, three sheets of heavy paper gone brown at the folds, written in a county clerk's copperplate so tight and curly it looks like lace. 'Daddy never could make out the back half,' she says. 'Neither could I. Granddaddy signed it with his mark.' You find the place two-thirds of the way down the second sheet, in the middle of a sentence that has been going on for half a page: 'provided always that any such shaft or opening abandoned by the said Company for the space of ten years shall revert, with the surface thereof, to the said grantor, his heirs and assigns forever.'

skillChecks.success: Abandoned 1916, on the company's own map. Ten years: 1926. The cap is Mavis's, and has been for a year. Whatever the sheriff signed is worthless.
skillChecks.failure: A lot of lawyer's language. It is about the shafts, somehow.

encounters: Ironwood men at the Gale depot and on the dead line (Night Watchman)
Six Ironwood men at the cap from Thursday 21 April (Night Watchman x6), on rotating shifts
An attempt on Friday 22 April's clear noon: possible, against the guards and the injunction, and the town not yet with the party

acts.title: Moving Day and the Last Night
acts.description: Saturday 30 April. The point of this act is to put the whole camp in one place, on Shumate's pasture round the cap, and give the Dark its last night. Moving day is hard and long and human: two hundred families on the road, the Local running it like a shift, the guards doing their job, the churches refusing. The last night is the campaign's horror finale: the camp sitting up together, the Dark hunting the lone, and the party's last chance to bring in the people who are still alone, including the superintendent.
objectives: Get the families up the ridge with their goods
Bring in everyone who is alone on the last night, including Bledsoe, the guards at the cap, Imre at the lamp house and Harley Mabe

scenes.name: Moving Day
scenes.description: From first light: the evictions, house by house; the Ford and the coal truck up and down the ridge road; tents going up in the rain on Shumate's pasture; Lettie's empty kitchen with the knocking going on under the floor; Rev. Greer in the door of Mount Moriah with a deputy and a warrant and two hundred people behind him. The party can be everywhere, and should feel that they can't.
scenes.readAloud: By noon the road down the hollow is a river of furniture. Bedsteads, stoves, trunks tied with rope, a cabinet organ on a wagon, a cow on a halter, chickens in a crate, a sewing machine carried between two men, old women riding on mattresses in Della's truck as it grinds up the ridge road in low gear, and the rain coming down on all of it. On the store porch Plumley stands with his ledger, writing down what each family still owes. At the head of the hollow the drift mouth is lit and the tipple is silent. And up on the ridge, in the upper pasture, round a fallen fence and a slab of concrete under a tarpaulin with six men in slickers standing on it, forty tents are going up in a ring.

skillChecks.success: You carry, all day, and nothing is lost or broken that you could reach. Union Trust +1.
skillChecks.failure: You carry all day and gain one level of exhaustion; something you could not reach is broken in the road.

skillChecks.success: (At Mount Moriah.) The deputy with the warrant looks at Rev. Greer, and the two hundred people, and the door of God's house, and folds his warrant and goes away.
skillChecks.failure: The deputy goes for help. The church holds until dark, and then it does not matter.

scenes.name: The Last Night
scenes.description: From dusk to dawn: the ovens banked, the plant cut, the camp in tents and churches, the Dark hunting. Run it as a sequence of voices and near things, with the party moving in pairs between the pasture, Mount Moriah, the lamp house and Silk Stocking Row, bringing people in. Garland at the cap. Bledsoe in his dark house. Imre at the Kept Light, if it is lit. Harley Mabe in the lamp house. Any player alone. Rev. Greer's Steady Now, Lettie's coffee, Clement's Treat Shock and the cook fires are the camp's defences; staying together is the only one that cannot fail.
scenes.readAloud: The dark comes up the hollow like water rising in a cellar. From the ridge you can watch it: the last orange of the banked ovens going out along the creek, the windows of the empty rows going dark, the drift-mouth bulbs flickering once and steadying, and then, house by house, the last few lights on Number Two Bottom going blue and small. Round you on the pasture forty lanterns and a dozen cook fires make a ring of light in the black, with the fence and the slab and the six guards' lantern in the middle of it. Somebody in a tent is singing a hymn, very quietly, and somebody else is singing the same tune in Hungarian. And from the black woods below the orchard, where nobody is, a young man's voice you know calls out: 'Vesta?' And then another voice, older, slower, with a Navy man's twang: 'Hensley? Garland? That you?'

skillChecks.success: It is using their voices because it wants you to come alone. You know the rule. You go in twos, with a light, and you bring someone back.
skillChecks.failure: They are calling for you, out there in the dark, the taken, and you could reach them if you went now, by yourself, quickly. Gain 1 Dread; and if you go alone, it is waiting.

skillChecks.success: (At Bledsoe's dark house on Silk Stocking Row.) He comes. He walks up to Mount Moriah between two of you, and sits by the stove where Rev. Greer puts him, among two hundred people, and does not sleep, and is not alone.
skillChecks.failure: He says he will stay where he is. He turns the lamp off when you leave. Someone has to go back.

encounters: The Hungry Dark, all night (adversaries.json; at full strength; it avoids company and bright light and takes the lone; it fights anyone who comes at it alone or tries to stop it taking someone, using Drink the Light first)
Frightened Townsmen in the tents, Jumpy, and a near-shooting of a guard who stumbles into the camp from the dark
Kincaid's advance men in No. 3, if the Kept Light holds it below: three men sent into 7 North a day early to start recovering material, one of whom is sent back alone for a tool

acts.title: Noon on Shumate Ridge
acts.description: Sunday 1 May. The point of this act is the laying, and the town standing together to do it. From first light: break the cap, in relays with sledges and bars, or a Sapper's charge after venting the gas; face Kincaid's six men with two hundred people and an old deed; get the pier glass up the ridge and on its frame; and at noon, throw the sun down the shaft. Then the fourteen come up.
objectives: Get past Kincaid's men without a massacre
Hold the glass steady and throw the sun down two hundred and twelve feet
Bring the fourteen up into the daylight, and name them

scenes.name: The Cap
scenes.description: First light, frost on the slab, six guards, two hundred people, the deed, the sledges. Kincaid arrives at seven with Philadelphia's telegram in his pocket. What happens depends on the scores, on whom the party saved, and on what they say. If Kincaid stands aside, the camp breaks the cap in relays, Black and white and Hungarian and Italian men and women taking turns with the sledges, the superintendent swinging one if he came up the ridge, and Garland Hensley laying the charge at the cracked corner if they use one. If Kincaid does not stand aside, the party must find a way that is not a battle.
scenes.readAloud: The first sledge comes down on the corner of the slab and rings like a bell. The frost jumps off the concrete in a white spray. Then the next, from a big man on the other side, and the next, in rhythm, the way men drive steel, and somebody starts to sing to keep the time, and the camp takes it up, two hundred people round a fallen fence on a ridge-top in the early sun, singing a work song to a slab of concrete. The six men in slickers stand at the edge of it with their rifles and do not know where to look. Captain Kincaid stands a little apart with his hands behind his back. On the slab, by your feet, the stamped letters go white with dust. O.S.C.Co. 10-17-19. At the third hour a crack runs right across them.

skillChecks.success: Kincaid reads the deed, and looks at the camp, and at his men, and at the telegram, and puts the telegram back in his pocket. 'This is not a company opening,' he says to his men. 'Stand down.' Advantage on this check if the party saved any of his guards, brought Lester Gaither out, or have the sheriff's rescission.
skillChecks.failure: Kincaid holds. Someone in the crowd has a rifle, too. The party have one round to put themselves between the two.

skillChecks.success: (A Sapper's charge, after venting.) The corner breaks clean and the slab goes in three pieces that can be levered off; the timbers below hold. Noon is an hour away.
skillChecks.failure: The slab breaks but a timber goes with it, and the hole is half choked; another hour of work with bars, and the glass has a narrower shaft to aim down.

scenes.name: Opened to the Sun
scenes.description: Eleven to one on the last clear noon. The pier glass on its frame of fence posts at the collar, two people holding it, someone sighting down the shaft and calling corrections. When the cap breaks, the voices come up the shaft (fear check DC 20). Holding the glass steady for the minute it takes is the check. Then the spot of sunlight goes down two hundred and twelve feet onto the floor of the barricade room, and it is over (see the secrets). Then the windlass, the fourteen brought up one by one, and their names said at the collar by people who knew them: Imre for József, Morris for Ezell, Rev. Greer for Moses, Lonzo for Lafe Combs, if he can.
scenes.readAloud: Two men hold the great glass on its frame of fence posts, and it is full of sky. Lonzo lies on his belly at the edge of the broken cap with his head over the black and calls: 'Left. Down. Down. Hold it.' And the sun goes into the glass, and out of the glass, a long bar of light down into the dark of the shaft, onto timbers that have not seen it in eight years, down, and down, and you cannot see the bottom, and then Lonzo says 'Oh,' in a voice none of you has ever heard him use. Out of the shaft comes a sound like a long breath let out, the whole mountain letting go of it. All round you on the ridge every lantern still burning in the daylight goes from blue to yellow at once. Far down at the head of the hollow, the drift-mouth bulbs burn steady. And from the bottom of the shaft, very faint and very far down, somebody knocks: four times, and twice. And then, for the first time since 1919, nobody does.

skillChecks.success: The light goes down and holds. It is laid. Everyone present drops to 0 Dread.
skillChecks.failure: The wind takes the glass and the light swings off the shaft; again, and quickly, before the sun moves off: a second try at DC 14, a third at DC 16, and after one o'clock the shaft is in shadow until the next clear noon, which is after the company goes in.

skillChecks.success: (When the cap breaks.) You hold on to the person next to you and you hold the glass and you don't look down the shaft.
skillChecks.failure: All of them, all at once, calling up out of the black for someone to come down. Gain 1 Dread, and the GM may let a player at Dread 5 or 6 choose to freeze; someone else must hold the glass.

encounters: Captain Kincaid and six Ironwood men at the cap (Deputy Sheriff, Night Watchman x6), and the crowd
The Hungry Dark below, in its room, which cannot come up into the sun: its voices up the shaft, and every lamp going blue, and nothing else

The fourteen Shades, after the laying: as each is brought up into the sun at the collar and named, those who knew them see him, for a moment, standing at the edge of the pasture with his lamp lit, and then not

rewards.money: The Herald pays Frankie $200 for the series and her editor's undying gratitude. Dr. Ketterly resigns his contract and is offered the practice in Gale by the county. The Local can pay nobody, but Union Trust 5 means the party never pay for a meal, a bed or a ride in Selden County again. Bledsoe's last act as superintendent, if he takes it, is to sign an order cancelling every bobtail balance owed to the store by a family of the fourteen.
items: Lafe Combs's notes, entered in a coroner's record, and the State's letter reopening the inquest of 1919 (if the jury added their rider)
The Herald's front page, and the wire stories that followed it
Fourteen brass checks, given back to the families with the men
The Kept Light, which Imre puts out himself, gently, with a snuffer, the evening after the laying, and gives to Morris

twists: If the Kept Light was relit and has held the Dark below since bd-scenario-002, the last night is quiet on the surface, and Kincaid's three advance men in 7 North are the ones in danger; one of them is sent back alone for a tool. Getting them out of the mine before dawn is the party's last night instead.

Garrett Ketterly, at the inquest, learns from the inspector's notebook that he drafted a lie in 1919, and in the middle of cross-examining Lonzo Cutright he stops, and asks the coroner for a recess, and in the recess tells his son that he will not oppose the rider. He keeps his client. He loses the case. He buys his son dinner.

Kincaid's last telegram from Philadelphia, which arrives on Saturday night and which he shows nobody, orders him to 'use all necessary means' to hold the cap. He has it in his pocket on the ridge. If the party have done what they could for his men, he never takes it out.
The last knock, four and two, up the shaft after the laying, is not a horror. It is the fourteen, answering, the way men answer when they hear the rescue party. Play it that way.
dmTips: The finale is not a fight with the Dark. It cannot be fought to an end, only laid, and the laying is a mirror on a ridge at noon. The tension is human: the guards, the deed, the law, the weather, the clock, and whether the camp holds together. Let the party's choices since 8 April decide how hard Sunday is.

The last night is the horror set piece and should be the scariest session of the campaign. The party are safe if they stay together. Everyone else is the question. Reward pairs running toward voices; let the camp see the party do it; by dawn the camp should be doing it too.

Do not let the confrontation at the cap become a battle unless the players insist, and if they do, make it what it would have been in 1927: a disaster the newspapers call a riot. The mine wars are real history and everyone on the ridge remembers them. The way through is the deed, the sheriff's rescission, Kincaid's men saved, and two hundred people standing still.

The real history: the union does not win in 1927, and the GM should not pretend it does. What the camp wins is its dead, brought up into the sun and named, the truth on the record, two men out of jail, and the memory of having stood together on the ridge. In 1933 the southern fields organise. Ottway's Local is the first in Selden County to sign.

Bringing the fourteen up is the campaign's real ending, and it can take a whole scene: the windlass, each man brought up into the sunlight, his name said at the collar by someone who knew him, and his family there. Ezell Pettaway's name is said by his brother, aloud, in front of the company. Give it time.

If the party fail on Sunday, Monday 2 May comes, and the company's crew goes into 7 North, and the GM should end the campaign on the drift mouth at dusk, with the night shift's lamps going blue one by one down the heading, and the first man sent back alone for a tool.
